name: LeBron James
philosophy: LeBron's edge is a freakish blend of size, speed and durability, built on a legendary year-round conditioning program. The focus: total-body power, elite recovery and a game that scores and creates from every spot on the floor.

name: Stephen Curry
philosophy: Curry redefined range with relentless shooting volume, blistering handle and neuromuscular training that sharpens balance and reaction. The blueprint is footwork, conditioning and thousands of makes on the move.

name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
philosophy: Giannis pairs a 7-foot frame with guard mobility, powered by explosive lower-body work and a huge focus on flexibility and length. Downhill attacks, transition finishing and two-way motor define his training.

name: Nikola Jokić
philosophy: Jokić's genius is footwork, touch and elite court vision over raw athleticism. The work centers on skill volume — passing reads, soft finishes and range — plus mobility to stay springy at his size.

name: Luka Dončić
philosophy: Luka overwhelms with pace changes, size at guard and a bottomless bag of step-backs. His prep leans on conditioning, deceleration control and shot creation off the dribble from all three levels.

name: Kevin Durant
philosophy: Durant is the purest scorer in the game — a 7-footer with a guard's stroke. Training is all about shooting mechanics, mid-range mastery and mobility to release cleanly over any contest.

name: Jayson Tatum
philosophy: Tatum's game grew from spot-up shooter to complete three-level scorer through obsessive skill work and added strength. The plan blends shot creation, footwork and two-way conditioning.

name: Victor Wembanyama
philosophy: Wembanyama is a generational unicorn — 7'4" with guard skills and rim-protecting length. His development focuses on mobility, strength to hold up inside, and perimeter skill work rare for his height.

name: Joel Embiid
philosophy: Embiid is a dominant two-way big with a guard's face-up game. The work: post footwork, mid-range and three-point touch, plus heavy strength and mobility to protect the paint.

name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
philosophy: Shai scores with rhythm, pace and elite touch inside the arc. His training emphasizes deceleration, mid-range mastery, ball control and the body control to draw contact and finish.

name: Ja Morant
philosophy: Ja is pure explosion — one of the most vertical guards ever. Training is built on plyometric power, first-step speed, body control in the air and ball-handling to attack downhill.

name: Devin Booker
philosophy: Booker is a silky pure scorer with footwork built on mid-range fundamentals. The plan focuses on shot creation off screens, pull-up shooting and conditioning to carry a heavy scoring load.

name: Anthony Edwards
philosophy: Edwards is a powerful, explosive two-way guard who plays above the rim. Training centers on lower-body power, defensive slides, and an improving pull-up and three-point stroke.

name: Anthony Davis
philosophy: Davis is a versatile two-way big who guards all five and scores inside and out. The work blends mobility, rim protection, face-up skill and strength management to stay durable.

name: Tyrese Haliburton
philosophy: Haliburton is a pace-and-space maestro whose passing runs an offense. Training emphasizes conditioning, quick-decision reads, transition speed and a clean, efficient jumper off the catch and dribble.

name: Jalen Brunson
philosophy: Brunson is a crafty low-to-the-ground scorer who wins with footwork and pace, not leaping. His blueprint is pivots, angles, change-of-speed handle and a reliable mid-range and floater.

name: Damian Lillard
philosophy: Lillard is a deep-range assassin with elite clutch nerve. His work is logo-range shooting volume, conditioning to shoot off the dribble late, and a tight handle to create space.

name: Kawhi Leonard
philosophy: Kawhi is a two-way machine with huge hands and relentless mid-range efficiency. Training centers on strength, footwork, defensive positioning and a compact, repeatable jumper.

name: Jimmy Butler
philosophy: Butler is a relentless competitor who thrives on conditioning, defense and getting to the line. His plan is high-volume strength work, footwork to the basket and a dependable mid-range.

name: Kyrie Irving
philosophy: Irving is arguably the best ball-handler and finisher ever, with a bottomless bag of layup packages. His work is elite handle reps, footwork and finishing at every angle.

name: Donovan Mitchell
philosophy: Mitchell is an explosive, compact scoring guard who plays above the rim. Training blends plyometric power, pull-up shooting and downhill attacks to score in bunches.

name: De'Aaron Fox
philosophy: Fox may be the fastest player in the league end to end. His blueprint is sprint speed, first-step quickness, transition finishing and a tightening pull-up jumper.

name: Trae Young
philosophy: Young is a floor general with deep range and elite passing vision. Training focuses on floaters, deep pull-ups, change of pace and reads to run pick-and-roll all night.

name: Zion Williamson
philosophy: Zion is a freight-train finisher with rare power and burst. His work centers on explosive strength, mobility, weight management and finishing through contact at the rim.

name: Paolo Banchero
philosophy: Banchero is a big forward who bullies mismatches and creates his own shot. Training blends strength, face-up footwork, ball-handling for his size and three-level scoring.

name: Bam Adebayo
philosophy: Adebayo is a switchable defensive anchor and hub passer. His plan is lateral quickness, hand-off and short-roll reads, plus an expanding mid-range and free-throw touch.

name: Karl-Anthony Towns
philosophy: Towns is one of the best shooting bigs ever — a true stretch center. His work is high-volume three-point shooting, post footwork and mobility to defend in space.

name: Paul George
philosophy: George is a prototypical two-way wing with size, shooting and on-ball defense. Training blends footwork, catch-and-shoot volume and lateral defensive work.

name: Jaylen Brown
philosophy: Brown is an explosive two-way wing who attacks downhill with power. His plan is first-step burst, finishing strength, handle tightening and a steadier jumper.

name: Jrue Holiday
philosophy: Holiday is one of the best perimeter defenders alive and a steady two-way guard. Training centers on defensive strength, conditioning and efficient shot selection.

name: Domantas Sabonis
philosophy: Sabonis is a double-double machine and elite passing hub. His work is footwork, rebounding positioning, hand-off reads and a growing perimeter touch.

name: Kristaps Porziņģis
philosophy: Porziņģis is a 7'3" unicorn who shoots threes and protects the rim. Training blends mobility, shooting mechanics at height and strength to hold up inside.

name: Franz Wagner
philosophy: Wagner is a big, skilled wing who creates and defends. His plan focuses on downhill driving, three-level scoring and improving his outside stroke.

name: Cade Cunningham
philosophy: Cunningham is a big lead guard with pace, size and vision. Training blends pick-and-roll reads, change of speed, finishing and pull-up shooting.

name: Alperen Şengün
philosophy: Şengün is a crafty modern big with elite touch and passing. His work is footwork, floaters, high-post reads and conditioning to run the offense.

name: Scottie Barnes
philosophy: Barnes is a jumbo point-forward who does a bit of everything. Training focuses on handle, playmaking reads, defensive versatility and a developing jumper.

name: Evan Mobley
philosophy: Mobley is a switchable defensive anchor with growing offense. His plan blends rim protection, mobility, face-up skill and shooting extension.

name: Jalen Williams
philosophy: Williams is a smooth two-way wing who scores and defends multiple spots. Training blends footwork, mid-range, on-ball defense and shooting off movement.

name: Chet Holmgren
philosophy: Holmgren is a unicorn big who shoots, protects the rim and runs the floor. His work is mobility, shooting mechanics and strength to hold up inside.

name: Tyler Herro
philosophy: Herro is a shot-making guard with deep range and shifty handle. Training centers on pull-up shooting, off-screen movement and conditioning to score in volume.

name: Zach LaVine
philosophy: LaVine is an explosive leaper and efficient three-level scorer. His work is plyometric power, catch-and-shoot volume and pull-up creation off the dribble.

name: DeMar DeRozan
philosophy: DeRozan is a mid-range maestro who lives in the mid-post. His blueprint is footwork, pivots, the mid-range pull-up and drawing fouls.

name: Pascal Siakam
philosophy: Siakam is a versatile forward with a spin-move signature and open-floor speed. Training blends footwork, transition finishing and three-level scoring.

name: Lauri Markkanen
philosophy: Markkanen is a 7-foot sharpshooter who spaces the floor and attacks close-outs. His plan is shooting volume, mobility and finishing off the drive.

name: Jamal Murray
philosophy: Murray is a clutch two-way guard with pick-and-roll mastery alongside Jokić. His work is pull-up shooting, floaters, conditioning and shot creation.

name: Darius Garland
philosophy: Garland is a shifty lead guard with a tight handle and deep range. Training blends ball-handling, floaters, pick-and-roll reads and quick-release shooting.

name: Brandon Ingram
philosophy: Ingram is a smooth long-limbed wing scorer with a soft mid-range. His work is footwork, pull-up shooting and using length to score over defenders.

name: Klay Thompson
philosophy: Thompson is one of the greatest catch-and-shoot snipers ever and a stout defender. His plan is off-ball movement, footwork into the catch and endless shooting reps.

name: Russell Westbrook
philosophy: Westbrook is one of the most explosive and relentless guards ever — the triple-double king. His work is elite conditioning, plyometric power and downhill attacking.

name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
philosophy: Jackson is a rim-protecting, floor-spacing modern big. Training blends vertical contest timing, mobility, three-point shooting and strength to defend inside.

name: Desmond Bane
philosophy: Bane is a strong, efficient shooting guard who scores at all three levels. His work is catch-and-shoot volume, pull-up creation and strength to finish through contact.

name: Mikal Bridges
philosophy: Bridges is a durable 3-and-D wing with elite conditioning. Training centers on catch-and-shoot shooting, on-ball defense and endurance to log heavy minutes.

name: OG Anunoby
philosophy: Anunoby is a powerful, switchable defender who spaces the floor. His plan is strength, lateral quickness, catch-and-shoot reps and finishing on drives.

name: Julius Randle
philosophy: Randle is a bruising lefty forward who bullies mismatches and passes well. Training blends strength, footwork, face-up handle and a reliable jumper.

name: Rudy Gobert
philosophy: Gobert is the premier rim protector of his era. His work is verticality, timing, conditioning to cover ground and screening plus lob-finishing efficiency.

name: Bradley Beal
philosophy: Beal is a smooth three-level scorer with a polished mid-range. Training centers on shot creation, pull-up shooting, footwork and conditioning to carry scoring loads.

name: Fred VanVleet
philosophy: VanVleet is an undrafted grinder and elite competitor at both ends. His work is conditioning, defensive toughness, deep shooting and steady playmaking.

name: Amen Thompson
philosophy: Thompson is a freak athlete and menace defender who plays above the rim. His plan is explosive power, defensive versatility, handle and a developing jumper.

name: Jalen Green
philosophy: Green is an explosive, high-flying scoring guard. Training blends plyometric power, first-step burst, pull-up shooting and finishing above the rim.

name: Dejounte Murray
philosophy: Murray is a long two-way guard with strong rebounding and passing. His work is defensive length, mid-range shooting and pick-and-roll playmaking.

name: CJ McCollum
philosophy: McCollum is a polished mid-range and pull-up shooter with tight footwork. Training centers on dribble-jumper craft, footwork and conditioning to score in volume.

name: Coby White
philosophy: White is a fast, streaky scoring guard with deep range. His plan is transition speed, pull-up shooting, conditioning and tightening playmaking.

name: Nikola Vučević
philosophy: Vučević is a skilled stretch-five with a soft touch and high-post passing. His work is footwork, mid-range and three-point shooting, plus rebounding positioning.

name: Josh Giddey
philosophy: Giddey is a jumbo playmaking guard who rebounds and passes at a high level. Training blends handle, transition reads, finishing and a steadier jumper.

name: LaMelo Ball
philosophy: Ball is a flashy, tall lead guard with deep range and elite vision. His work is handle creativity, deep pull-ups, transition passing and conditioning.

name: Brandon Miller
philosophy: Miller is a smooth big wing with three-level scoring upside. Training blends shot creation, catch-and-shoot volume, footwork and finishing on drives.

name: Deni Avdija
philosophy: Avdija is a big, physical point-forward who defends and pushes the pace. His work is handle, transition finishing, playmaking reads and shooting.

name: Shaedon Sharpe
philosophy: Sharpe is a explosive leaper with scoring flashes. Training centers on plyometric power, pull-up shooting, handle and finishing above the rim.

name: Derrick White
philosophy: White is a two-way connector who shoots, defends and blocks shots as a guard. His work is catch-and-shoot volume, defensive timing and conditioning.

name: Immanuel Quickley
philosophy: Quickley is a quick, shifty combo guard with deep range. Training blends pull-up shooting, floaters, conditioning and pick-and-roll playmaking.

name: RJ Barrett
philosophy: Barrett is a strong, downhill lefty wing who attacks the rim. His plan is finishing strength, footwork, handle and a steadier outside shot.

name: Zach Edey
philosophy: Edey is a massive, old-school interior force. His work is footwork, screening, rebounding positioning, conditioning and finishing efficiency at the rim.

name: Jabari Smith Jr.
philosophy: Smith is a long, floor-spacing forward who defends multiple positions. Training blends shooting mechanics, mobility, strength and defensive versatility.

name: Draymond Green
philosophy: Green is the ultimate defensive quarterback and connective passer. His work is conditioning, defensive IQ and communication, switchability and playmaking from the elbow.

name: Michael Porter Jr.
philosophy: Porter is a tall, elite catch-and-shoot forward and strong rebounder. His work is shooting volume, footwork off screens and finishing on drives.

name: Cam Thomas
philosophy: Thomas is a fearless shot-maker who scores in bunches. Training centers on tough-shot creation, pull-up shooting, footwork and conditioning to carry a load.

name: Nic Claxton
philosophy: Claxton is a mobile, switchable rim-runner and shot-blocker. His plan is verticality, lateral quickness, lob finishing and conditioning to guard in space.

name: Aaron Gordon
philosophy: Gordon is a powerful two-way forward and elite lob finisher. Training blends explosive power, defensive versatility, cutting timing and a steadier jumper.

name: Christian Braun
philosophy: Braun is a high-motor two-way wing who cuts, defends and finishes. His work is conditioning, cutting reads, catch-and-shoot volume and transition finishing.

name: Andrew Wiggins
philosophy: Wiggins is a smooth two-way wing with length and athleticism. Training centers on shot creation, catch-and-shoot shooting, on-ball defense and finishing.

name: Norman Powell
philosophy: Powell is a strong, efficient scoring guard who catches fire quickly. His work is catch-and-shoot volume, downhill finishing strength and conditioning.

name: Austin Reaves
philosophy: Reaves is a crafty combo guard who scores, passes and draws fouls. Training blends handle, floaters, pull-up shooting and pick-and-roll reads.

name: Rui Hachimura
philosophy: Hachimura is a strong, efficient forward with a reliable corner three. His plan is strength, catch-and-shoot volume, footwork and finishing on drives.

name: Deandre Ayton
philosophy: Ayton is a mobile, skilled big with a soft mid-range and strong rebounding. Training blends footwork, pick-and-roll finishing, rebounding and mid-range touch.

name: Kyle Kuzma
philosophy: Kuzma is a versatile scoring forward who works all three levels. His work is shot creation, footwork, catch-and-shoot volume and finishing.

name: Bobby Portis
philosophy: Portis is a high-energy stretch big who rebounds and shoots. Training blends rebounding positioning, catch-and-shoot volume, strength and conditioning.

name: Myles Turner
philosophy: Turner is a stretch-five and elite shot-blocker. His plan is verticality, timing, three-point shooting and mobility to defend the rim and the perimeter.

name: Tyrese Maxey
philosophy: Maxey is a lightning-fast guard with deep range and a great motor. Training centers on speed, pull-up and catch-and-shoot volume, conditioning and playmaking.

name: Jalen Duren
philosophy: Duren is a young, powerful lob-finisher and rebounder. His work is verticality, screening, rebounding positioning, conditioning and finishing efficiency.

name: Jaden Ivey
philosophy: Ivey is an explosive, downhill guard with elite burst. Training blends first-step speed, transition finishing, handle and pull-up shooting.

name: Tobias Harris
philosophy: Harris is a durable, efficient forward who scores at all three levels. His plan is footwork, mid-range and catch-and-shoot volume, and finishing.

name: Keegan Murray
philosophy: Murray is a floor-spacing forward who defends and shoots. Training blends catch-and-shoot volume, footwork, defensive versatility and finishing.

name: Malik Monk
philosophy: Monk is an explosive microwave scorer off the bench. His work is pull-up and catch-and-shoot volume, plyometric power, handle and conditioning.

name: Jonathan Kuminga
philosophy: Kuminga is a powerful, explosive forward who attacks the rim. Training blends explosive power, finishing strength, handle and a developing jumper.

name: Buddy Hield
philosophy: Hield is a relentless off-ball sniper with deep range. His plan is off-screen movement, footwork into the catch, conditioning and endless shooting reps.

name: Devin Vassell
philosophy: Vassell is a smooth two-way wing with a clean jumper. Training centers on catch-and-shoot and pull-up volume, footwork, and on-ball defense.

name: Stephon Castle
philosophy: Castle is a big, physical two-way guard with defensive upside. His work is handle, downhill finishing, defensive versatility and a developing jumper.

name: Herbert Jones
philosophy: Jones is a lockdown perimeter defender with a reliable corner three. His work is lateral quickness, defensive length and timing, plus catch-and-shoot volume.

name: Dyson Daniels
philosophy: Daniels is a long, disruptive point-of-attack defender they call 'The Great Barrier Thief.' His work is defensive hand timing, lateral quickness, conditioning and a steadying jumper.

name: Cooper Flagg
philosophy: Flagg is a two-way phenom with rare feel, motor and versatility for his age. Training blends explosive power, defensive reads, handle for his size and shot development.

name: Jalen Suggs
philosophy: Suggs plays like a point guard trapped in a strong safety's body, closing passing lanes and bodying up ball-handlers before turning steals into transition offense. His training leans hard into lateral quickness drills and on-ball defensive footwork to fuel a two-way game built on relentless effort.

name: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope
philosophy: A decade-plus of guarding the other team's best perimeter scorer has made KCP a walking clinic in positional defense, chasing shooters through screens without wasted motion. Offensively he stays a low-maintenance floor spacer, drilling catch-and-shoot threes off named actions rather than needing the ball in his hands.

name: Wendell Carter Jr.
philosophy: Carter's game is built on footwork over flash, a skilled post scorer who can also step out and hit the occasional mid-range jumper. He treats box-outs and post positioning like a craft, using leverage and timing rather than pure size to control the glass.

name: Anthony Black
philosophy: Black's calling card is size at the point of attack, using his 6'7" frame to see over defenses and smother ball-handlers a position up. His development is centered on shooting mechanics and pace control, sharpening the parts of his game that still lag behind his defensive instincts.

name: Jonathan Isaac
philosophy: When healthy, Isaac is a rim-protecting unicorn who can switch onto guards and still contest at the basket a possession later. His entire regimen is built around durable, sustainable movement patterns after years of injury rehab, prioritizing joint health as much as explosiveness.

name: Jalen Johnson
philosophy: Johnson's breakout came from turning raw athleticism into a genuine point-forward toolkit, grabbing the rebound and pushing it himself. His training emphasizes ball-handling under fatigue and explosive first-step drills to keep exploiting mismatches in the open floor.

name: Onyeka Okongwu
philosophy: Okongwu wins with quickness for his size, hedging pick-and-rolls and recovering to the rim faster than most bigs can dream of. He trains like a guard trapped in a center's body, prioritizing agility work and hip mobility to stay a switchable, versatile defensive anchor.

name: Nickeil Alexander-Walker
philosophy: NAW has carved out a role as a pesky, physical point-of-attack defender who can guard multiple positions and still knock down catch-and-shoot threes. His work centers on active hands and anticipation drills, turning deflections into easy offense.

name: Alex Caruso
philosophy: Caruso built a career out of doing the unglamorous things at a max-effort level, ripping steals and taking charges that swing momentum. His training is defense-first: reaction time drills and film study over highlight-reel athleticism, proving hustle is a repeatable skill.

name: Isaiah Hartenstein
philosophy: Hartenstein is the connective tissue of a modern offense, a true passing big who can facilitate from the elbow and short roll. He trains for touch and vision as much as strength, treating the dribble hand-off and skip pass like extensions of his own scoring game.

name: Luguentz Dort
philosophy: Built like a linebacker, Dort makes a living absorbing contact and still contesting shots without fouling out. His conditioning program emphasizes core strength and contact tolerance, letting him bang with forwards a weight class above him possession after possession.

name: Aaron Wiggins
philosophy: Wiggins thrives in the gaps of a stacked roster, moving without the ball and knocking down open looks created by better-known teammates. His approach is efficiency over volume, refining shot selection and off-ball timing rather than forcing a bigger role.

name: Cason Wallace
philosophy: Wallace is a defense-first connector who already guards the toughest perimeter assignment on a title-contending roster. He trains around discipline and positioning, a young player who has learned to make winning plays before chasing box-score stats.

name: Jaylen Wells
philosophy: Wells emerged as a smooth, low-drama scorer who fills the box score without needing plays run for him. His training is heavy on catch-and-shoot reps and defensive positioning, refining a game built to complement stars rather than compete with them.

name: Santi Aldama
philosophy: Aldama's stretch-four skill set lets him pop for threes or attack closeouts off the bounce, a rare blend of size and handle. His training stresses perimeter shooting volume and change-of-direction work to keep exploiting mismatches against slower bigs.

name: Ty Jerome
philosophy: Jerome runs an offense with veteran calm, probing defenses off the dribble before hitting the right read. His work emphasizes footwork and change of pace, using craft and deception rather than raw speed to get where he wants on the floor.

name: Ivica Zubac
philosophy: Zubac has quietly become one of the league's most efficient interior scorers, finishing lobs and put-backs with soft touch around the rim. His training is old-school big-man fundamentals: post footwork, positioning for boxouts, and conditioning to stay effective across heavy minutes.

name: James Harden
philosophy: Harden reinvented shot creation with his signature step-back three and mastery of drawing contact, forcing defenses into impossible choices. His training is built around hip mobility and change-of-pace deception, sustaining an isolation-heavy game deep into his 30s.

name: Bogdan Bogdanović
philosophy: Bogdanović brings a European-honed feel for the game, reading defenses a beat ahead and firing off movement threes with a quick release. His training leans on footwork off screens and passing under pressure, skills sharpened over years of international competition.

name: Brook Lopez
philosophy: Lopez reinvented himself late in his career as a stretch-five rim protector, spacing the floor with high-arcing threes while still anchoring the paint on defense. His longevity comes from a maintenance-focused regimen built around joint care and verticality drills for shot-blocking without fouling.

name: Donte DiVincenzo
philosophy: DiVincenzo plays with a fearless, all-effort motor, sprinting the floor for transition threes and diving for loose balls without hesitation. His training centers on conditioning and quick-trigger shooting mechanics, keeping his energy level identical in the first and fourth quarters.

name: Naz Reid
philosophy: Reid gives Minnesota rare size-shooting combination off the bench, capable of popping for threes or bullying smaller closeouts inside. His training blends perimeter shooting volume with post-up strength work, making him a matchup nightmare in short bursts.

name: Mike Conley
philosophy: Conley has run winning offenses for nearly two decades on the strength of clean decision-making and a quietly deadly floater. His longevity secret is meticulous recovery and body maintenance, allowing him to still change speeds and stay in front of younger guards.

name: Jaden McDaniels
philosophy: McDaniels' length and fluid hips let him guard point guards and power forwards in the same series without missing a step. His training focuses on wingspan-driven perimeter defense and improving a still-developing jumper to match his defensive ceiling.

name: Rob Dillingham
philosophy: Dillingham's game is shifty and score-first, using a live handle to create separation for pull-up jumpers most guards his size can't get to. His development is focused on adding strength and improving decision-making as he grows into a bigger role.

name: Nikola Jović
philosophy: Jović brings guard-like passing vision in a forward's frame, initiating offense from the elbow and pushing pace in transition. His training emphasizes ball skills and shooting range, developing the tools to become a full-time point-forward.

name: Terry Rozier
philosophy: Rozier has built a career on fearless shot-making, unafraid to pull up from deep in isolation situations late in games. His training centers on core strength and off-the-dribble shooting reps, keeping his pull-up jumper reliable under contest.

name: Kel'el Ware
philosophy: Ware pairs rim-running verticality with surprising touch, running the floor like a wing before finishing above the rim. His training targets explosiveness and shot-blocking timing, sharpening the raw physical tools that made him an instant rotation piece.

name: Jaime Jaquez Jr.
philosophy: Jaquez plays an old-soul, footwork-heavy game, using pump fakes and euro-steps to create angles most young wings skip past. His training leans into balance and body control drills, refining the craft that let him translate college production immediately to the NBA.

name: Collin Sexton
philosophy: Sexton is a downhill attacker who never met a contested layup he didn't like, using explosive first-step burst to collapse defenses. His training is built around finishing through contact and improving pull-up range to keep pressuring defenses off the dribble.

name: Miles Bridges
philosophy: Bridges combines explosive vertical athleticism with a legitimate stretch shot, capable of posterizing defenders one possession and popping for three the next. His training emphasizes power output and jump mechanics, maintaining a highlight-reel level of bounce.

name: Grant Williams
philosophy: Williams built his career on being a smart, physical connector who can switch screens and still knock down a corner three. His training is heavy on strength and lateral quickness work, letting an undersized forward hold up against bigger post players.

name: Daniel Gafford
philosophy: Gafford is a rim-running lob threat who converts nearly everything at the basket and protects it just as fiercely on the other end. His training focuses on explosive vertical pop and timing for shot-blocking, keeping his efficiency near the top of the league.

name: P.J. Washington
philosophy: Washington's game is defined by positional flexibility, sliding between the four and five while stretching the floor from deep. His training blends strength work for post defense with perimeter shooting volume, keeping him valuable in any lineup configuration.

name: Max Christie
philosophy: Christie has grown into a reliable three-and-D wing, moving well without the ball and closing out hard on shooters. His training centers on catch-and-shoot repetition and defensive slide mechanics, the unglamorous work that keeps him on the floor.

name: Walker Kessler
philosophy: Kessler is a paint-clogging shot-blocker who alters shots without ever leaving his feet early, reading angles a step ahead of drivers. His training is centered on verticality and timing drills, maximizing rim protection without foul trouble.

name: Keyonte George
philosophy: George plays with a fearless scorer's mentality, pulling up from deep in transition and probing pick-and-rolls with shifty handles. His training emphasizes shot selection and pace control, tightening up the decision-making around his natural scoring instincts.

name: Kyle Filipowski
philosophy: Filipowski offers a modern big's skill package, passing from the elbow and stepping out for threes rather than living solely in the post. His training focuses on perimeter shooting reps and improving foot speed to defend on the perimeter as well as the block.

name: Isaiah Collier
philosophy: Collier is a bulldozing downhill playmaker, using strength and vision to get into the paint and set up teammates. His training is focused on outside shooting development, the missing piece that would unlock his full point-guard ceiling.

name: Ausar Thompson
philosophy: Thompson is a defensive playmaking machine, generating steals and blocks with freakish length and closing speed. His training leans on explosive athleticism and transition conditioning, fueling a game built on getting rim-runs off turnovers he creates himself.

name: Ron Holland II
philosophy: Holland's energy and length make him disruptive on both ends before his offensive game has even matured. His training focuses on jump-shot mechanics and ball-handling reps, building the polish to match his defensive motor.

name: Jose Alvarado
philosophy: Alvarado is pure chaos for opposing ball-handlers, full-court pressuring and gambling for steals with fearless intensity. His training is built around lateral quickness and anaerobic conditioning, sustaining that pressure defense for every second he's on the floor.

name: Trey Murphy III
philosophy: Murphy has grown from a specialist shooter into a legitimate scoring wing, attacking closeouts off the catch with real explosiveness. His training pairs high-volume three-point shooting with vertical explosiveness work, expanding his game beyond spot-up duty.

name: Yves Missi
philosophy: Missi's calling card is relentless activity around the rim, sprinting the floor and finishing above defenders on pure motor. His training targets strength and hands work, building the interior polish that will let his natural energy translate into a bigger role.

name: Andrew Nembhard
philosophy: Nembhard is a steady operator who reads the whole floor before he ever picks up his dribble, a low-turnover engine for a fast-paced offense. His training emphasizes decision-making under pressure and pick-and-roll footwork, the foundation of his no-nonsense point-guard game.

name: Bennedict Mathurin
philosophy: Mathurin plays with a scorer's swagger, attacking off the catch and finishing through contact in transition. His training is built around explosive first-step work and shot volume, fueling an aggressive downhill game off the bench or in the starting five.

name: Aaron Nesmith
philosophy: Nesmith has developed into a tenacious three-and-D wing, sprinting the floor for corner threes and locking down the other team's top scorer. His training pairs spot-up shooting volume with defensive slide work, keeping him a reliable two-way piece.

name: Toumani Camara
philosophy: Camara has become a defensive stopper ahead of schedule, guarding multiple positions with physicality and relentless closeouts. His training emphasizes strength work and shooting reps, rounding a defense-first game into a more complete two-way profile.

name: Donovan Clingan
philosophy: Clingan is a mountain in the paint, deterring drives with sheer size and mopping up defensive rebounds in traffic. His training is built around foot speed for a big man and post-move footwork, sharpening the offensive game to match his defensive presence.

name: Scoot Henderson
philosophy: Henderson's game is built on blow-by burst, using elite first-step quickness to get into the paint at will. His training focuses on jump-shot consistency and pick-and-roll reads, refining the pieces around his game-breaking speed.
